races.name: Weatherbys Racing Bank Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Runman
runners_data.note: Clear class advantage as a previous winner with hold-up style perfectly suited to expected race shape

runners_data.name: Hattie's Comet
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced newcomer from low-percentage trainer making debut assessment impossible
runners_data.comment: 62,000gns yearling out of a 7f/1m winner (Listed); heed the market signals
runners_data.spotlight: 62,000gns yearling out of a 7f/1m winner (Listed; RPR 100) and half-sister to French winners Spherical (7f) and I Am Incredible (5.5f); best watched unless the betting suggests otherwise.

runners_data.name: Vitality
runners_data.note: Front-runner who showed stamina reserves when third at Southwell but faces stronger opposition
runners_data.comment: Went down by 3l in a five-runner 1m Southwell maiden (16-1) after making the running
runners_data.spotlight: Went down by 3l in a five-runner 1m Southwell maiden (16-1) after making the running; a 3yo filly taking on the males but could prove the main threat to Runman.

runners_data.name: Get Outta Here
runners_data.note: Prominent runner ideally positioned to benefit if pace-setters overdo it early
runners_data.comment: Beaten in the region of 7l at Deauville (7f) and Kempton (1m)
runners_data.spotlight: Beaten in the region of 7l at Deauville (7f) and Kempton (1m); likely to be seen in a better light when handicapping.

runners_data.name: Thomas Picton
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with concerning fade pattern but racing in much weaker company than recent Newbury effort
runners_data.comment: 65,000euros yearling; 66-1 when 18th of 25 in a 1m Newbury maiden ten days ago
runners_data.spotlight: 65,000euros yearling; 66-1 when 18th of 25 in a 1m Newbury maiden ten days ago; this race has far less depth.

runners_data.name: Fizzy Bear
runners_data.note: Another hold-up type who should appreciate the stronger pace and step up in trip
runners_data.comment: Modest fifth at Kempton before finishing just ahead of Thomas Picton at Newbury
runners_data.spotlight: Modest fifth at Kempton before finishing just ahead of Thomas Picton when both were down the field at Newbury ten days ago.

runners_data.name: Hengest
runners_data.note: Struggling hold-up horse making stable debut for new trainer after disappointing Yarmouth effort
runners_data.comment: Three runs for three different yards; finished last at Yarmouth only recently
runners_data.spotlight: Bought for £1,800 after one run for Andre Fabre; beaten 28l in one run over hurdles for Jamie Snowden and was last at Yarmouth on recent stable debut (1m).

runners_data.name: Mick The Hat
runners_data.note: Backmarker who has shown little ability in two all-weather starts for Ralph Beckett
runners_data.comment: Handicaps could beckon after this following down-the-field runs on the AW
runners_data.spotlight: Handicaps could beckon after this following down-the-field runs on the AW (at about 1m; 16-1/80-1).

runners_data.name: Pureis King
runners_data.note: Front-runner with clear fade issues who looks outclassed despite bumper win
runners_data.comment: Bumper winner but well beaten in two 1m races on the Kempton AW
runners_data.spotlight: Bumper winner but well beaten in two 1m races on the Kempton AW and unlikely to be winning this.

races.paceDynamic: Vitality and Pureis King will force the early pace with both showing clear front-running tendencies, though Pureis King has a concerning fade pattern that may see him weaken. Get Outta Here will likely track the leaders prominently while the majority of the field including Runman, Thomas Picton, Fizzy Bear, Hengest and Mick The Hat will settle towards the back. With two confirmed pace-setters over this stamina-testing trip at Epsom, the early gallop should be honest but may not be overly strong given the small field size. This race shape clearly favours hold-up horses who can finish strongly, as the pace-setters are vulnerable to being picked off in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is honest but not overly strong with Vitality and Pureis King leading
scenarios.body: The pace-setters will soften up the race perfectly for the closers, with Runman's class and Fizzy Bear's stamina coming to the fore in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Get Outta Here can position perfectly behind the leaders without being involved in the early battle
scenarios.body: The David Menuisier-trained gelding will have the ideal pitch to strike when the front-runners tire, avoiding both the early pace and getting trapped behind horses.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Lasts Home
scenarios.trigger: If Vitality gets an uncontested lead with Pureis King failing to go the pace early
scenarios.body: The Charlie Johnston filly will be able to dictate throughout and may have enough stamina at this longer trip to hold off the closers despite her 3lb penalty.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If both Vitality and Pureis King go off too conservatively creating a sprint finish
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace will turn this into a dash from the two-furlong pole, potentially suiting any horse with a turn of foot regardless of usual running style.

watchPoints.text: Pureis King may set unsustainably strong fractions early given his front-running style before predictably fading
Thomas Picton showed nothing at Newbury but drops significantly in class and could outrun his odds
Hattie's Comet represents an expensive yearling purchase making debut for connections with limited recent success
Get Outta Here has tactical speed to sit closer than usual if the pace becomes modest
Runman returns from a 208-day break but the Gosden stable excel with horses returning from long layoffs

races.name: Betfred Blue Riband Trial Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Balzac
runners_data.note: Front runner making debut at this trip with strong staying pedigree but may face early pressure from Menzies.
runners_data.comment: Lots to like about 1m Newmarket debut; didn't need to improve to win 1m AW novice
runners_data.spotlight: Winning siblings include Claymore, a Group 3 winner at 1m2f for this yard; lots to like about his persevering third of seven in a good 1m Newmarket maiden (22-1; ridden by 7lb claimer) on debut but he didn't need any more than that form when making all on Kempton AW (1m) this month; Derby entry who should make a better 3yo but how much better will be clearer after today.

runners_data.name: Saxon Street
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse from powerful Gosden stable returning after 131 days with excellent stamina breeding for this distance.
runners_data.comment: 170,000euros yearling; came home strongly when winning AW debut (1m); new trip will suit
runners_data.spotlight: 170,000euros yearling; unraced dam's winning siblings include Raheen House (1m5f; Group 3) and Shraaoh (Australian 2m Group 1); a warm order for Chelmsford AW debut (1m) in December and although workmanlike rather than impressive in beating rivals who mostly look handicappers in the making, he did finish with purpose; should leave that form well behind over a more suitable trip for yard that's won five of the last ten runnings; entered in the Dante and the Derby.

runners_data.name: New Zealand
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with proven class and Group-race experience, ideally suited to Epsom's unique demands under Ryan Moore.
runners_data.comment: Close up in Group 3 in October; fair 5th in French Group 1 after; good claims up in trip
runners_data.spotlight: By Frankel; dam won the Group 3 Albany (6f) as 2yo and bred Group-placed Agenda (1m4f) for this yard; clung on for 7f maiden win at the Curragh on second start but was a better horse in the autumn, not having much to race against when involved in a scramble for second in a Group 3 at Newmarket (1m, good to firm) then bogged down by the class rise and/or very soft ground in the Group 1 Criterium International at Saint-Cloud; likely to do better as a 3yo over this longer trip; good chance with sights lowered.

runners_data.name: Rebel Rocker
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who won convincingly on debut but faces significant step up in class after 160-day absence.
runners_data.comment: Made a good impression when winning AW debut (1m) but the bare form was ordinary
runners_data.spotlight: Derby entry; nibbled at in the market for 1m debut on Kempton AW in November where he made a good impression with the way he made up ground to win quite convincingly; his rivals had some limitations though and although this one should improve he is asked a big question today.

runners_data.name: Menzies
runners_data.note: Front runner who relishes making the running but trainer Harry Eustace has poor recent strike rate of 0/10.
runners_data.comment: Wide-margin winner of 1m AW novice on 2nd start; needs plenty more than subsequent defeat
runners_data.spotlight: One sibling was a Graded winner at 1m3f and 1m1f in US; took a step forward from 7f debut on Kempton AW when making the running and not for catching over 1m there in February; had more to do under a penalty at Southwell since and he fell short so now relies on big improvement for the step up in trip.

runners_data.name: Pearl River
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose best form comes on good ground or softer with stamina proven over this trip.
runners_data.comment: Stout staying win in 1m2f handicap (good to soft) on final 2yo start; much more needed
runners_data.spotlight: All five races on good or slower; middling form on first three starts but was all the better for the step up to 1m2f on final two runs and his stamina was much in evidence when forging clear in a Nottingham handicap (good to soft), despite running green; needs to have come on a ton over the winter to play a part and the track and good to firm ground are other queries.

races.paceDynamic: Balzac and Menzies are confirmed front runners who will contest the early lead, setting up an honest gallop from the start. With limited pace in a small field, the tempo may be steady rather than fierce through the middle sections. The stamina-laden 1m2f trip at Epsom's unique undulating track will expose any lack of staying power in the closing stages. This honest pace scenario strongly favours prominent racers and hold-up horses who can finish, disadvantaging pure speed types who need softer fractions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace between Balzac and Menzies creates steady fractions through halfway
scenarios.body: Saxon Street, New Zealand and Rebel Rocker get perfect tactical setups to unleash finishing kicks up Epsom's demanding hill. The patient riders can time their challenges perfectly when the front runners begin to tire.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front runner survives
scenarios.trigger: If Balzac or Menzies can secure an uncontested lead with the other settling behind
scenarios.body: The leader gets first run on the field and maintains enough in reserve to hold off late challengers on the climb to the line. Honest pace but not suicidal fractions allow the pacesetter to last home.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent racer strikes
scenarios.trigger: If New Zealand can secure the ideal stalking position just behind the early leaders
scenarios.body: Ryan Moore can track the pace and pounce when the front runners falter, using New Zealand's proven class and Frankel stamina to grind out victory. The Ballydoyle runner has the tactical speed to quicken when needed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace collapses completely
scenarios.trigger: If both Balzac and Menzies go too fast early or one refuses to lead
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish where pure class tells over stamina, suiting horses with high cruising speed regardless of running style. This scenario would be chaotic and unpredictable for all concerned.

watchPoints.text: Balzac and Menzies could go too fast early if both refuse to give way, setting up back-runners perfectly.
Saxon Street returning after 131 days without a recent run for fitness, though Gosden stable excellent with returnees.
New Zealand showed disappointing effort last time at Leopardstown and needs to bounce back to best form.
Rebel Rocker stepping up significantly in class after winning a weak Kempton maiden on debut.
Pearl River has raced exclusively on good ground or softer, making conditions ideal for another bold showing.

races.name: Lilley Plummer Risks City & Suburban Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Sallaal
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist returning from 191-day layoff faces tough task with limited early pace to aim at
runners_data.comment: Made it 3-4 at Hamilton last July; his progress then stalled but he retains potential
runners_data.spotlight: Made it three wins from his first four starts when scoring on handicap debut at Hamilton (8.3f, good) last July; his progress stalled in two Listed races subsequently but this lightly raced 4yo has been gelded since and the return to better ground could be a positive, along with the step up in trip; retains potential for a top trainer who won this in 2018 and 2019; respected.

runners_data.name: Rathgar
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in career-best form following recent Newbury success, ideally placed to track Aurel
runners_data.comment: Last year's runner-up who won at Newbury ten days ago; solid contender
runners_data.spotlight: Beat 13 rivals to win at Newbury (1m2f, good) ten days ago on his second start back from some time off; back up 4lb but he's just 1lb higher than when second in this last year and he's a solid contender.

runners_data.name: Aurel
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner returning from lengthy absence but gelded since, should control tempo without pressure
runners_data.comment: Absent since Royal Ascot last June; 2-3 previously and may well have more to offer
runners_data.spotlight: Absent since midfield finish in Golden Gates Handicap at Royal Ascot (1m2f, good to firm) last June; gelded since; however, he was 2-3 previously, the wins coming in a maiden at Kempton (1m, AW) and a novice at Leicester (1m2f, good to firm), and he may well have more to offer for his respected trainer.

runners_data.name: Parlando
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with recent turf return showing promise but trainer Ian Williams struggling with 0/27 14-day record
runners_data.comment: 3rd of eight at Pontefract when back on turf; suspicion that he might find a few too good
runners_data.spotlight: Two AW wins in December and returned to turf with 3l third of eight at Pontefract (1m2f, good) last Tuesday; might not be far away but there's a suspicion that this exposed 7yo might find a few too good; cheekpieces go on.

runners_data.name: Asmen Warrior
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent runner with excellent recent form, well-suited to press forward behind leaders
runners_data.comment: Runner-up on four of his five starts since joining this yard and he's not discounted
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up last July-October on three of his first four starts for this yard and he again finished second on this month's reappearance at Thirsk (1m4f, good), albeit no match for the winner; he could build on that latest effort and is not discounted.

runners_data.name: Duke's Command
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse stepping back up to 1m2f after AW success, needs strong pace to be effective
runners_data.comment: Raced wide when sixth of 14 at Newcastle; remains unexposed at 1m2f and not ruled out
runners_data.spotlight: Won at Lingfield (AW) in December on first crack at 1m2f and raced wide when sixth of 14 at Newcastle (1m2f, AW) last month; this two-time turf winner remains unexposed at today's trip and is not ruled out.

runners_data.name: Dangerman
runners_data.note: Prominent type returning from 200-day break but previous blinkers-on form at this trip is compelling
runners_data.comment: Improved for these blinkers last summer and could rediscover progressive ways on comeback
runners_data.spotlight: Won two in a row at Sandown (1m2f, good) last summer when these blinkers went on and third there (1m2f, soft) next time; appeared unsuited by the step up to 1m4f at Newmarket in October; this lightly raced 4yo is in excellent hands and could rediscover his progressive ways with a big run today.

races.paceDynamic: Aurel stands as the sole confirmed front-runner and will dictate terms from the start, with Rathgar, Asmen Warrior and Dangerman likely to press forward early but settle behind the leader. The absence of genuine speed pressure means Aurel can control fractions and avoid being harried into unsustainable splits. With prominent runners like Rathgar and Dangerman likely to track closely, the pace should be honest but not brutal, setting up a scenario where horses need to be handy to strike. This race shape strongly favors prominent runners and those with tactical pace over pure hold-up horses, as the controlled tempo will make it difficult for back-markers to close ground effectively.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front Running
scenarios.trigger: If Aurel dictates reasonable fractions without serious early pressure
scenarios.body: The Ralph Beckett-trained gelding can utilize his class advantage and kick clear in the straight while prominent trackers struggle to match his sustained drive. His 311-day absence is mitigated by the lack of pace pressure allowing him to find his rhythm.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Rathgar or Dangerman get ideal stalking positions behind Aurel
scenarios.body: The controlled pace allows these tactical types to conserve energy before unleashing finishing kicks, with Rathgar's recent Newbury win and Dangerman's blinkers-on form making them dangerous. Their fresher conditions give them the edge in a sustained drive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Surges
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes pedestrian and opens up the back straight
scenarios.body: Hold-up horses like Sallaal and Duke's Command get the perfect setup to unleash devastating late runs, though they need everything to fall right. The sustained nature of Epsom's climb still makes this challenging despite the tactical advantage.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Aurel goes too slowly and multiple horses challenge simultaneously
scenarios.body: The race becomes a messy sprint finish where any horse with a turn of foot can capitalize, favoring those with recent race fitness. Fresh legs and tactical positioning matter more than running style in this chaotic finale.

watchPoints.text: Aurel's 311-day absence could see him blow up in the straight despite controlling the early pace
Watch Dangerman's early positioning as his blinkers-on record at 1m2f is excellent but needs to be handy
Rathgar's recent Newbury win came after a break, suggesting he handles fresh returns well
Multiple hold-up horses may struggle if Aurel sets modest fractions with no genuine pace pressure
Asmen Warrior has been runner-up in four of his last five starts and looks overdue for breakthrough win

races.name: Weatherbys Global Stallions App Great Metropolitan Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Night Breeze
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with solid Epsom form who should track Topteam comfortably but may lack the finishing kick of his main rivals
runners_data.comment: Sound surface and 1m4f ideal; back in form lately, including at Musselburgh on Sunday
runners_data.spotlight: Not disgraced in last year's Northern Dancer over C&D (good; likely softer) on sole start here; also won twice at Ascot (good to firm) last term; back to form on last two starts, latterly when beaten 2l at Musselburgh (also 1m4f, good) on Sunday; should make his presence felt.

runners_data.name: Asgard's Captain
runners_data.note: Last year's course winner returns fresh under Egan with proven 1m4f effectiveness and ideal prominent style for tracking the leader
runners_data.comment: Won this last year; arrives fit after creditable efforts in UAE and must be considered
runners_data.spotlight: Last year's winner (good) who ran well in two other appearances over C&D; did well to win at York (1m4f, good to firm) under John Egan in August and arrives here fit after three creditable efforts at Meydan; firm contender.

runners_data.name: Sing Us A Song
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 214-day break under James Doyle faces traffic concerns in small field but arrives fresh for Beckett
runners_data.comment: Winning 1m2f return last year; signed off with another win (1m6f) in September; unexposed
runners_data.spotlight: Won heavy-ground Goodwood maiden at two and it was a convincing success on last year's reappearance/handicap debut at Sandown (1m2f, good) one year ago; disappointed at Royal Ascot and Glorious Goodwood subsequently but had been gelded when back on the scoresheet at Haydock (1m6f, good to soft) in September; drops in trip for this comeback but not fully exposed.

runners_data.name: Topteam
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner with three good ground wins gets ideal scenario to control pace but must prove gelding operation hasn't dulled his finishing kick
runners_data.comment: Scrapper who won three times on turf last term and again on AW return; tops the list
runners_data.spotlight: Really likeable sort who scored three times on good ground (1m2f/1m4f) last term, twice coming out on top in tight finishes; gelded before again showing a fine attitude to pick up Kempton handicap (1m4f, AW) on his reappearance three weeks ago; likely won't go down without a fight for his ever-growing fan club.

runners_data.name: Nunc Est Bibendum
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare stepping back from 2m success faces tactical challenge but carries lowest weight and brings stamina advantage
runners_data.comment: Secured AW hat-trick up at 2m over the winter; something to prove at this trip on turf
runners_data.spotlight: Ex-Irish mare who secured an AW hat-trick once upped to 2m across December and January but suffered odds-on reversal when dropped to 1m6f in bid for the four-timer; drops further in trip returned to turf (had form on grass in Ireland) on this first start for three months; others more persuasive.

races.paceDynamic: Topteam will set a steady tempo from the front with no natural early challenger, creating an uncontested lead scenario. Night Breeze and Asgard's Captain will settle prominently behind the leader, while Sing Us A Song and Nunc Est Bibendum drop back to pick up pieces. With only five runners and Topteam able to dictate fractions, this becomes a test of who can best utilize the tactical positioning behind the leader. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners who can track the pace and strike, as hold-up horses face limited opportunities to weave through traffic in such a small field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Topteam Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Topteam maintains his recent form and gets soft fractions on the front end
scenarios.body: Oisin Murphy can dictate ideal splits and kick clear turning for home, making the hold-up horses' task near impossible. The gelded four-year-old's three wins on good ground last season prove he handles these conditions perfectly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Night Breeze or Asgard's Captain can get the jump on Topteam in the straight
scenarios.body: The race becomes a straight fight between the two prominent runners, with last year's winner Asgard's Captain holding a slight edge through course experience. Night Breeze's Ascot wins suggest he has the class to capitalize if positioned perfectly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes genuinely slow and Sing Us A Song gets a clear run from James Doyle
scenarios.body: The Ralph Beckett-trained four-year-old can utilize his fresh legs after 214 days off to produce a devastating late surge. His Sandown handicap debut win proved his effectiveness when getting racing room.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Topteam stops in front and creates a messy finish with multiple challengers
scenarios.body: The small field becomes bunched turning for home, allowing any horse to capitalize on the moderate early pace. Nunc Est Bibendum's stamina advantage from recent 2m wins could prove decisive in a slowly-run affair.

watchPoints.text: Topteam breaking slowly or being challenged early would completely alter the pace dynamic and favor the closers
Night Breeze and Asgard's Captain getting too close to each other in running positions, reducing their tactical options
Sing Us A Song's fitness levels after 214 days off, as any rustiness will be exposed in this small competitive field
Weather changes affecting the good ground, as several runners have mixed records on softer surfaces
Oisin Murphy's early positioning on Topteam, as any deviation from front-running tactics would create chaos

races.name: Betfred 'Nifty 50' Handicap

runners_data.name: Timber Twelve
runners_data.note: Unbeaten front-runner with 38 days off, but faces much stronger pace pressure than in previous wins
runners_data.comment: 2-2 and brings plenty of potential to this turf/handicap debut; must be considered
runners_data.spotlight: Overcame a wide stall when springing 28-1 surprise at Kempton in September and kept unbeaten record when defying a penalty on his return at Southwell (also 1m, AW) five weeks ago; will likely be going up in trip soon enough but brings plenty of potential to this turf/handicap debut.

runners_data.name: On Message
runners_data.note: Long absence of 204 days is a concern despite her making-all Wolverhampton success
runners_data.comment: Promise on turf; made all on AW in October; interesting on reappearance and handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Promise on first two starts (good to firm/soft) and she made all on AW debut at Wolverhampton (7f) in October; should do better at this trip and beyond (holds Oaks and Irish Oaks entries) this term; interesting on her reappearance and handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Mayaada
runners_data.note: Course winner but tailed off badly last time and needs to rediscover her August form
runners_data.comment: Course maiden (7f, good) winner last term but seems to have lost her form; down the list
runners_data.spotlight: Busy as a juvenile when her nine runs yielded one win; that did come here (7f, good) in August but was quiet on last two starts and virtually tailed off on last month's AW comeback; return to this venue might help, and a handicapping case can be made, but otherwise has plenty to prove.

runners_data.name: Terranoble
runners_data.note: Hold-up style perfectly suited to expected pace scenario but making turf debut
runners_data.comment: All starts around 1m on AW; improved to win January novice; respected on turf/h'cap debut
runners_data.spotlight: All starts around 1m on AW; only made his debut in December but that was an eyecatching effort and he improved on third start to land Wolverhampton novice in January; potential to do better again on this turf/handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Assaranca
runners_data.note: Made all when winning at Nottingham but will face much fiercer pace battle here
runners_data.comment: Nursery winner; can be excused easy-ground reappearance over 1m2f; not readily dismissed
runners_data.spotlight: Off the mark on her eighth start as a juvenile when landing Nottingham nursery (good, made all) over this trip in October; not disgraced in Listed company next time but weakened over 1m2f (good to soft) on her reappearance one month ago; might do better back at this distance with the run behind her.

runners_data.name: Montague Menace
runners_data.note: Recent gelding operation has sparked improvement and his closing style suits the race shape
runners_data.comment: Gelded when winning AW maiden last month; should have more to offer on handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Gelded ahead of his AW debut when readily landing Lingfield maiden (7f) on last month's return; will probably need more on this switch back to turf/handicap debut but it's still early days and he warrants consideration.

races.paceDynamic: Timber Twelve, On Message, and Assaranca will all go forward from the bell, creating a genuine three-way battle for the early lead over Epsom's testing 1m½f trip. This sustained gallop will stretch the field and put maximum emphasis on stamina, particularly as they climb Tattenham Hill and face the camber. The strong pace will set up the race for horses with proven staying power who can finish strongly. This race shape heavily favours the hold-up horses who can conserve energy and pick up the pieces when the pace-setters tire.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Late
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners go too hard early and crack climbing the hill
scenarios.body: The sustained battle between Timber Twelve, On Message and Assaranca will take its toll as they hit Tattenham Hill, allowing the closers to sweep up. Terranoble and Montague Menace are perfectly positioned to exploit the pace collapse with their hold-up styles.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one of the pace-setters can rate themselves better than their rivals
scenarios.body: Timber Twelve's unbeaten record suggests he can judge pace better than On Message and Assaranca, potentially stealing a march as the others weaken. His recent Southwell success shows he can handle pressure and find extra when challenged.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Mayaada can sit just off the pace and avoid the early battle
scenarios.body: The Epsom course winner can use her track knowledge to position perfectly behind the leading trio before making her move. Her previous success here gives her a tactical advantage that could prove decisive if she can recapture her best form.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos In Running
scenarios.trigger: If the pace battle causes interference or significant trouble in running
scenarios.body: The narrow Epsom track combined with three keen front-runners could cause traffic problems that shuffle the pack completely. Any horse finding clear water at the right moment could capitalize on others' misfortune.

watchPoints.text: Timber Twelve may not get the soft lead he enjoyed in previous victories with On Message and Assaranca both wanting to dominate
On Message's 204-day absence could catch up with her if the pace becomes truly testing up Tattenham Hill
Mayaada's last two runs were poor and she needs to prove the course advantage can overcome recent form decline
Terranoble makes his turf debut but his hold-up style is perfectly matched to the likely race development
The three confirmed front-runners could go so fast early that even 1m½f becomes a stamina test

races.name: Betfred 'In Celebration Of Mark Friar' Handicap

runners_data.name: Kaleido
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who will set the early pace but faces pressure from multiple hold-up horses on this tactical track
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and retains potential ahead of this seasonal/stable debut; has been gelded
runners_data.spotlight: Placed on soft and fast ground in his first three maidens (7f/1m) before landing the odds with comfortable win at Yarmouth (7f, good) in July; made favourite for handicap debut but weakened to finish ninth at Glorious Goodwood (1m, heavy; Knights Gold third) a fortnight later; bought for 21,000gns in October and subsequently gelded; retains plenty of potential ahead of this seasonal/stable debut.

runners_data.name: Mr Baloo
runners_data.note: Strong hold-up performer back on turf after AW win, cheekpieces retained, perfectly suited to modest early pace
runners_data.comment: 7f nursery winner here who won (AW) in cheekpieces last time; retains handicapping scope
runners_data.spotlight: 7f nursery winner here (good; has won on good to firm) in 2023; landed seventh AW win when scoring at Lingfield (1m; first-time cheekpieces, retained) a fortnight ago; has won off higher marks than this and must be considered on his return to turf.

runners_data.name: Sweet Reward
runners_data.note: Veteran prominent runner returning after 185 days, may find trip on short side but going suits
runners_data.comment: This trip is on the short side but he won on last year's reappearance and is 2lb lower
runners_data.spotlight: Seven wins include five off higher marks than this and one at this track (1m2f, good to soft; has won on good) in 2023; this trip might be on the short side but he went close on his reappearance in 2024 (1m2f) and scored off 2lb higher on his comeback last term (1m2f); not readily dismissed.

runners_data.name: Knights Gold
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up horse with five wins this year, unlucky last time and well-suited to this race shape
runners_data.comment: Productive last year but yet to get going this term; mark demands a return to his peak
runners_data.spotlight: Five handicap wins (7f to 1m; four in a hood) in a productive 2025, including on a fast surface, and he looked unlucky when third of 15 at Glorious Goodwood (1m, heavy; Kaleido ninth) in July; probably needed reappearance in March and likely didn't stay 1m2f when never competitive three weeks later; this mark demands a return to his best, though.

runners_data.name: Organ
runners_data.note: Hat-trick winner returning after 220 days off, just 2lb above last winning mark with strong course form
runners_data.comment: Landed hat-trick last term before form tailed off; nothing wrong with this mark on return
runners_data.spotlight: Completed a hat-trick over 7f/1m on good/good to firm across May and June last year; form tailed off markedly from August onwards but he returns just 2lb above his last winning mark; market support would bring him into the picture.

runners_data.name: Carnival Day
runners_data.note: Course winner who ran well in this race last year, hold-up style suits expected pace scenario
runners_data.comment: 1m2f winner here in July; this trip raises a question on return; market might help
runners_data.spotlight: Respectable fourth in the Great Metropolitan on last year's card; one win last year but it did come here in July and he was a respectable second at this track (also 1m2f, good to soft; has won on good) in September; below par over 1m on his final start in October and this trip again asks a question; market might help ahead of his comeback.

runners_data.name: Amused
runners_data.note: Ex-French gelding with prominent tendencies, headgear retained after recent placed efforts
runners_data.comment: Solid AW fifth in December; cheekpieces on for this return and he's not ruled out
runners_data.spotlight: Ex-French gelding who was unraced at two; made all to land Vichy claimer (very soft) in August and went mighty close for this yard in Leicester seller (good) in October; 25-1 and raced wide before solid fifth of 12 at Kempton (also 7f, AW) when last seen in December; cheekpieces enlisted for second go at this sort of trip and he's not ruled out on return.

runners_data.name: Tribal Rhythm
runners_data.note: Won this race last year from off the pace, well-suited to repeat tactical scenario
runners_data.comment: Last year's winner who looked unlucky when second on this month's comeback; every chance
runners_data.spotlight: Returned from seven months off to win this race from off the pace last year; couldn't build on that in four subsequent starts last season but was back down to that winning mark when slightly unlucky second at Bath (1m, also good) on his resumption three weeks ago; of firm interest.

runners_data.name: Shafdar
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in good current form, Ian Williams stable struggling but horse shows ability

runners_data.name: Tronido
runners_data.note: Course winner in hood, lowest-rated but gets weight relief and suits hold-up tactical angle
runners_data.comment: Knows how to win but little encouragement in three starts this term; mark fine
runners_data.spotlight: Four-time winner who won at Sandown in August and followed up by 6l over C&D (soft; acts on good) in September; just 2lb above that latter winning mark but there hasn't been much encouragement in three AW starts this term.

races.paceDynamic: Kaleido and Sweet Reward will set a modest early tempo from prominent positions, with Amused also likely to race handily. The hold-up brigade of Mr Baloo, Knights Gold, Organ, Carnival Day, Tribal Rhythm, Shafdar and Tronido will all be looking to come from off the pace on this downhill finish. With limited early pace and a strong downhill run-in at Epsom, this race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can produce their best work late. The patient tactics will be rewarded as the pace will build gradually rather than being honest throughout.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace remains modest as expected with only Kaleido and Sweet Reward showing early
scenarios.body: The lack of genuine pace will allow the closers to get into perfect striking positions turning for home, with Epsom's downhill finish suiting their style perfectly. Multiple hold-up horses will be in contention in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Hold On
scenarios.trigger: If Kaleido or Sweet Reward can dictate at a sensible tempo without being pressured early
scenarios.body: Either can maintain their advantage as the field closes late, taking advantage of the tactical race and their superior positions throughout. The pace won't be strong enough to completely expose their prominent tactics.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Surge Develops
scenarios.trigger: If multiple hold-up horses get squeezed for room or come too late in their challenges
scenarios.body: The pace will still be modest but the sheer number of closers creates traffic problems and allows one to get first run. Some talented hold-up horses will be unlucky but others benefit from cleaner passages.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If Kaleido and Sweet Reward go too slowly and create a sprint finish from the turn
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure test of acceleration rather than stamina, potentially suiting horses with tactical pace. This scenario makes the form hard to assess and creates upset potential.

watchPoints.text: Sweet Reward may struggle to see out this trip after 185 days off despite her class advantage
Watch early pace development - if Kaleido goes too slow it creates a sprint finish that changes everything
Mr Baloo's first run back on turf since winning - cheekpieces retained suggests connections confident
Knights Gold needs luck in running given hold-up style and competitive field of similar tactical horses
Tribal Rhythm attempting to repeat last year's winning tactics in identical race conditions
